judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: News-teaser photo in the NEWS group (not a link). The crop shows an empty pub interior: bar, chequered floor, wooden chairs. The alt is the story headline, 'Fight on to save busy Wetherspoons in the North East as pub's future in doubt', and the same headline follows as an h3 link. claimTrue yes: the campaign to save the pub and its uncertain future are not shown; only the pub interior is. captureDiffers no: the snapshot caught the lazy image before it loaded (height 0), but the screenshot shows the small teasers with their photos, and the alt and src match the live HTML. The live page (fetched 2026-11-21) has the same markup: the img sits in its own cover div, not in a link, followed by the h3 headline link, with alt equal to the headline. Competent auditors split on this news-teaser pattern: one reading says the photo is informative and an alt that repeats the headline neither describes it (G94) nor is null as a redundant or decorative image should be, so 1.1.1 fails; another accepts the headline as an alternative that serves the image's purpose in the teaser (illustrating that story), since the picture adds nothing the user needs. My own reading leans to a failure, but the disagreement is real and no rubric rule settles it, so the label is uncertain. If it fails, the claim names that failure: the alt describes the story, not what the picture shows.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Header image (Chronicle 'C' logo plus the word SUBSCRIBE) that is the only content of a link to /subscribe. The link carries aria-label 'Subscribe to premium membership'. claimTrue yes: 'nechronicle' is a site label and does not convey the SUBSCRIBE button the image shows. But the control is the link, and its name, set by aria-label, describes its purpose; that name, not the alt, is what assistive technology announces. 1.1.1 asks a control to have a name that describes its purpose (Situation C, ARIA6/G82), which is met. The ACT rule qt1vmo leaves out images with an ancestor named from author ('ignored because it is a child of a link that provides its accessible name'). alt='' would be cleaner, but the element does not fail. captureDiffers no: the button is rendered client-side (absent from the server HTML for every visitor) and the screenshot shows it as captured. Rampa judged the image's alt as if it named the control.
